title: "Olfactory Commodification and the 'By Mennen' Jingle as Miniature Kulturindustrie"

abstract: "The 'By Mennen' jingle is a seemingly innocuous audio memory for people of a certain age from the United States. We revisit this jingle as a paradigmatic instance of what we term 'compressed ideological acoustics' as a miniature kulturindustrie: the audio capacity of late-capitalist advertising to embed commodity relations within the mnemonic architecture of everyday life. Past scholarship on this frontier had been focused on the visual spectacle of consumer culture and has given relatively little attention to two- or three-word auditory fragments. Drawing on critical theory, and an unnecessarily elaborate reading of deodorant commercials from the 1980s/1990s, we argue that the persistence of 'By Mennen' in the minds of Americans of a certain age reveals the hidden durability of the culture industry. The jingle's reappearance is not experienced as memory properly understood, but as a form of involuntary recall in which the subject discovers that a corporation has been living rent-free in their head since the Cold War. The article concludes that that recognition of the jingle serves as an informal demographic sorting mechanism. Those who immediately hear the melody are compelled to confront a troubling realization of their mortality and the urgency of monitoring daily vitamin intake. The phrase 'By Mennen' functions simultaneously as a brand identifier, a mnemonic fossil, and a gentle reminder that it may be prudent to discuss calcium supplementation with a healthcare professional."
